A reel; a device around which thread, wire or cable is wound, especially a cylinder or spindle.

examples.text: If you need to reload film, the cassette can be rewound slightly by turning the hub located on one end of its spool.

glosses: One of the rotating assemblies of a gas turbine engine, composed of one or more turbine stages, a shaft, and one or more compressor or fan stages.

examples.text: The high-pressure spool rotates faster than the intermediate- and low-pressure spools, as the high-pressure turbine is driven by superheated combustion gases straight out of the burners, while the high-pressure compressor has to spin very fast to compress air that has already been compressed and heated by the low- and intermediate-pressure compressors.

glosses: A temporary storage area for electronic mail, etc.

To wind on a spool or spools.
To send files to a device or a program (a spooler or a daemon that puts them in a queue for processing at a later time).

A spool or cylinder around which wire is coiled.

examples.text: Ignition coils using a bobbin molded from high-performance polyester withstand open-circuit bench tests to 70kV.

glosses: In a sewing machine, the small spool that holds the lower thread.

examples.text: Wind the bobbin, place it in the machine, and raise the thread.

glosses: The little rounded piece of wood at the end of a latch string, which is pulled to raise the latch.

examples.text: She went from the linhay and boldly pulled the bobbin of the fuel-house door.
